title: Al Pastor Marinade

ingredients.name: Chipotle Peppers
ingredients.notes: dried; or substitute 0.5 tsp chipotle powder

steps: Toast and de-seed the dried guajillo chilies, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes and drain.

Blend soaked guajillos (with a splash of soaking liquid) together with chipotle, pineapple juice, orange juice, apple cider vinegar, garlic, onion, achiote paste, ancho powder, oregano, cumin, paprika, brown sugar, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
While blending on low, slowly drizzle in olive oil to emulsify the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning; optionally stir in fresh lime juice for extra tang.
Marinate thinly sliced pork (or chicken, tofu, etc.) in the sauce, refrigerating at least 4 hours or overnight.
Grill, broil, or pan-sear the marinated protein until caramelized and cooked through. Serve on warm corn tortillas with pineapple chunks, cilantro, onion, and a squeeze of lime.
notes: If only chipotle powder is available, use 0.5 tsp. For a thinner sauce add extra pineapple juice. Vegetarian option: use jackfruit or portobello mushrooms. The sauce stores in the fridge up to 2 weeks or frozen in ice-cube trays.

Assemble crisp and bake for 45-60 minutes.
Cool for 20-30 minutes.

title: Black Forest Energy Balls
steps: Place dates and dried cherries in a small heatproof bowl; cover with boiling water. Let stand until soft, about 10 minutes. Drain well.

Place the drained dates and cherries in a food processor; pulse until coarsely chopped, about 5 pulses. Add almond butter, yogurt, cocoa, vanilla and salt. Pulse until incorporated, 5 to 10 pulses. Add oats; pulse until fully combined and incorporated, about 15 pulses. (Add 1 tablespoon water if the mixture is too thick and stiff.) Transfer the mixture to a medium bowl. Cover and refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon of the date mixture onto a sheet of wax paper or parchment paper; roll into a 1-inch ball. Repeat with the remaining date mixture.
Melt dark chocolate in double boiler
Drizzle the balls with the melted chocolate; sprinkle with cinnamon. Refrigerate, uncovered, until set, at least 10 minutes.

title: Cherry Pistachio Protein Balls
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together {{Almond Butter}}, {{Tahini}}, and {{Honey}} until smooth and thoroughly combined.
Stir in {{Vanilla Protein Powder}} and {{Ground Flaxseed}} until fully incorporated.

Fold in {{Rolled Oats}}, chopped {{Pistachios}}, and chopped {{Dried Cherries}}. Mix thoroughly until a uniform, thick dough forms. (If too crumbly, add 1-2 teaspoons of honey or water; if too sticky, add an extra tablespoon of oats.)
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for 20-30 minutes to firm up the dough and allow the oats and flaxseed to absorb moisture.
Scoop about 1 tablespoon of dough at a time and roll firmly between your palms into 1-inch balls.
If desired, melt {{Dark Chocolate}} in the microwave or a double boiler and drizzle over the balls. Refrigerate for 10 minutes to set the chocolate.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1-2 weeks, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Cranberry Walnut Protein Balls
steps: In a medium bowl, stir together {{Peanut Butter}} and {{Honey}} until smooth and thoroughly combined. (If the peanut butter is firm, microwave for 10-15 seconds to soften.)
Stir in {{Vanilla Protein Powder}} and {{Chia Seeds}} until incorporated.

Fold in {{Rolled Oats}}, {{Walnuts}}, and {{Dried Cranberries}}. Mix thoroughly until a thick, uniform dough forms. (If too crumbly, add 1-2 teaspoons of honey, peanut butter, or warm water; if too sticky, add an extra tablespoon of oats.)
Cover and chill in the refrigerator for 20-30 minutes to make the dough easier to handle and allow the chia seeds and oats to absorb moisture.
Scoop about 1 tablespoon of dough at a time and roll firmly between your palms into 1-inch balls.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1-2 weeks, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Mexican-Style Pinto Beans (Instant Pot)

ingredients.name: Dried Pinto Beans
ingredients.notes: rinsed and sorted, no soaking needed

ingredients.name: Chicken Broth
ingredients.notes: or vegetable broth to keep vegetarian

ingredients.name: Jalapeño or Chipotle
ingredients.notes: halved, seeds removed for less heat

ingredients.name: Dried Epazote
ingredients.notes: optional but traditional; substitute dried oregano

steps: Rinse and sort the dried pinto beans, discarding any shriveled beans or debris. No soaking is required.
Set the Instant Pot to Sauté (Normal). Add lard or olive oil and heat until shimmering.
Add the halved onion cut-side down and the smashed garlic cloves. Sauté for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant.
Add the cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and Mexican oregano. Stir and cook for 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Pour in the chicken broth and water, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Add the rinsed pinto beans, jalapeño, bay leaves, and epazote (if using). Stir to combine. Do NOT add salt yet — it can toughen the bean skins.
Secure the lid, set the vent to Sealing, and cook on Manual / Pressure Cook (High) for 45 minutes.
Allow the pressure to release naturally for 20 minutes, then carefully quick-release any remaining pressure.
Remove and discard the onion halves, jalapeño, and bay leaves.
Stir in the salt, taste, and adjust seasoning. For creamier beans, use a wooden spoon or potato masher to smash about one-quarter of the beans against the side of the pot.
Serve topped with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime juice.
notes: Salt is added after cooking — adding it beforehand can prevent beans from fully softening. If your beans are very old (over a year), increase cook time to 50–55 minutes. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 5 days and freeze well for 3 months. Use these as a base for refried beans by mashing and frying in a skillet with a little lard or oil.

title: Smoky Turkey Chili

ingredients.name: Chipotle Pepper
ingredients.notes: homemade smoked and frozen; character is similar to a rehydrated dried chipotle — minced or finely diced

ingredients.name: V8 Juice
ingredients.notes: 12 oz each (36 oz total); yields a soupier chili that thickens with simmering

ingredients.name: Mexican Oregano
ingredients.notes: large pinch; added in the last 5 minutes of simmering to preserve its bright, citrusy aroma

ingredients.name: Cayenne Pepper
ingredients.notes: optional; omit for a mild batch, include for the spicy competition version

steps: Dice {{Poblano Pepper}} and mince or finely dice {{Chipotle Pepper}}. In a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat, cook the peppers together with {{Ground Turkey}}, breaking up the meat, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7–10 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
Add {{Pre-Minced Garlic}} and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in {{V8 Juice}} and stir to combine.

Add {{Ground Cumin}}, {{Onion Powder}}, {{Ancho Chili Powder}}, {{Guajillo Powder}}, {{Chili Powder}}, {{New Mexico Chili Powder}}, {{Paprika}}, {{Salt}}, and {{Black Pepper}}. If making the spicy competition batch, add {{Cayenne Pepper}} as well. Stir to fully incorporate.
Add the drained {{Light Red Kidney Beans}}, {{Dark Red Kidney Beans}}, and {{Black Beans}}. Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chili thickens to your liking.
Stir in {{Mexican Oregano}} and simmer for a final 5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

title: Thanksgiving Roasted Sweet Potatoes with Cinnamon Glaze

ingredients.name: Sweet Potatoes
ingredients.notes: about 4 medium, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Part-Skim Ricotta
ingredients.notes: cold, drained in a fine mesh strainer for 15 minutes if watery

ingredients.name: Orange Zest
ingredients.notes: from about half a large orange

ingredients.name: Fresh Thyme
ingredients.notes: optional, leaves only, for a subtle savory note

steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, toss {{Sweet Potatoes}} with {{Olive Oil}}, 2 tablespoons of {{Maple Syrup}}, {{Ground Cinnamon}}, {{Ground Nutmeg}}, {{Kosher Salt}}, and {{Black Pepper}} until evenly coated.

Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet, leaving space between pieces. Roast for 20 minutes, flip each piece, then roast for another 15–20 minutes until caramelized on the edges and tender through the center when pierced with a fork.

While the sweet potatoes roast, make the whipped ricotta topping: combine {{Part-Skim Ricotta}}, the remaining 1 tablespoon of {{Maple Syrup}}, {{Vanilla Extract}}, and {{Orange Zest}} in a food processor or blender. Process for 60–90 seconds until completely smooth and fluffy. Taste and stir in {{Powdered Sugar}} if desired. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast {{Pecans}}, stirring frequently, for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Remove from heat immediately and set aside.
When the sweet potatoes come out of the oven, transfer them to a serving platter. Dollop or spread the whipped ricotta over the top.
Scatter {{Dried Cranberries}} and toasted {{Pecans}} evenly over the dish. Garnish with {{Fresh Thyme}} leaves if using. Serve warm.

title: Turkey Burgers with Japanese BBQ Sauce

ingredients.name: Green Onions
ingredients.notes: thinly sliced (white and green parts separated)

steps: Preheat grill, grill pan, or cast-iron skillet to medium-high heat.

In a large bowl, combine the {{Ground Turkey}}, {{Panko Breadcrumbs}}, beaten {{Egg}}, white parts of the sliced {{Green Onions}}, minced {{Garlic}}, grated {{Fresh Ginger}}, {{Soy Sauce}}, {{Toasted Sesame Oil}}, {{Salt}}, and {{Black Pepper}}.

Gently mix the ingredients together with your hands until just combined (do not overwork, or the burgers will be dense). Form the mixture into 4 equal-sized patties, about 3/4-inch thick. Press a slight dimple in the center of each patty to prevent them from puffing up while cooking.
Lightly oil the cooking surface. Cook the patties for about 5-6 minutes on the first side. Flip, then brush the cooked side generously with {{Japanese BBQ Sauce}}.

Cook for another 4-5 minutes on the second side, brush the second side with more {{Japanese BBQ Sauce}}, and continue cooking until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C). Remove patties and let them rest for 5 minutes.
While patties are resting, toss the {{Shredded Cabbage}} with the {{Rice Vinegar}} and a pinch of salt to make a quick slaw.

Assemble the burgers: spread {{Kewpie Mayonnaise}} on the toasted {{Brioche Buns}}. Place a turkey patty on each bottom bun, top with the dressed {{Shredded Cabbage}} slaw, sprinkle with the green parts of the {{Green Onions}} (and sesame seeds if desired), brush with a little extra {{Japanese BBQ Sauce}}, and cover with the top bun. Serve hot!
